# [bug][ibex_decoder] Report a bug in Ibex
Hi all!
I am using a static analysis to found a various bugs in open source RTL designs.
It was founded that in `ibex_decoder.sv` RTL file dead code is exists [here](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/master/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv#L439).
This assignment under `else` statement is never executed due to [this](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/master/rtl/ibex_decoder.sv#L406) external `else` branch with `!instr[26]` condition.

<analysis>
The reported issue is about dead code in `rtl/ibex_decoder.sv`:

- In the `3'b101` decode path, there is an outer `if (instr[26])` branch at lines 404–405.
- Inside the corresponding `else` branch, there is a `5'b0_0001` case for `unshfl`.
- That case contains an inner `if (instr[26] == 1'b0)` at lines 436–437 and an `else` at 438–439.
- Because execution only reaches this `case` when `instr[26]` is already `0`, the inner `else` is unreachable dead code.

This suggests the primary location is the decoder logic itself, but the issue should be reviewed in all corresponding decode/execute paths to ensure consistency:

1. The decode-time legality check in `ibex_decoder.sv` contains the unreachable branch.
2. The ALU/control-generation path in the same file contains functionally similar logic for the same instruction family (`unshfl` / immediate bit-manipulation) and may need consistency review.
3. Since this is decoder behavior, any mirrored or parallel handling in other stages or variants should be checked for the same condition pattern.

Relevant locations in the provided snippets:
- `rtl/ibex_decoder.sv` lines 403–444: the exact reported dead-code region.
- `rtl/ibex_decoder.sv` lines 901–933: analogous ALU decode handling for the same `3'b101` immediate bit-manipulation group.
- `rtl/ibex_core.sv` lines 370–415 and 421–489: context for decoder integration and signal flow, useful to confirm that no downstream logic depends on the unreachable branch.

No other provided snippet shows the same exact unreachable condition, but the closely related ALU decode path should be inspected for consistency with the legality decode path.
